correctness.rationale: All 32 distinct length-five factors require hits, each mark covers five, so at least seven marks. Exactly 384 seven-mark subsets hit every length-five window (7 positive gaps at most five with deficits totaling three). For any such subset, coverage of the 30 shorter factors is necessary and sufficient for all circular factors. A standalone exhaustive checker enumerates all 65536 permissible five-state successor permutations and their 2048 single cycles; independent four-state Euler-tour generation returns the exact same set. All 2048 cycles admit at least 216 of the 384 candidates. The extreme frequencies 4 and 2 and sum 589120 are computed exhaustively. Each selected witness is checked by reconstructing literal short factors; extremal examples are checked at all factor lengths.

value.rationale: The question whether the unique order-five-factor packing lower bound can be attained across every de Bruijn cycle is mathematically natural in circular data compression, and a 2024 primary paper raises the general problem. The result settles its exact binary order-five circular case without assuming a special construction and quantifies the redundancy of optimal position sets. It is a complete finite theorem with an explicit exhaustive certificate, not a recomputation of the 2048 known cycle count. No higher-order consequence is asserted.
